generatedBy: npm run verify (scripts/verify.mjs) — all numbers fetched live; verdicts derived by the thresholds in that file

verdictScale.Survives: The claim's numbers hold up against independent live data.
verdictScale.Inflated: A real kernel (benchmark, later peak, gross figure) is presented as more than the data supports.
verdictScale.False: The claim is contradicted by the data — in C2's case, arithmetically impossible.
verdictScale.Unverifiable: No independent public source can test the claim; exactly what is missing is stated on the card.

claims.claim: NEAR Intents has crossed $37B+ in all-time volume with 37M+ swaps
claims.test: Rebuild cumulative settled Intents volume from an independent aggregator (DefiLlama) and compare against $37B; check the swap-count leg against the lifetime transaction count of the intents.near contract on NearBlocks.
claims.justification: Independent rebuild matches the headline: DefiLlama's cumulative NEAR Intents volume is $37,005,533,919 (100.0% of the claimed $37B). The gross number survives. Caveat the headline omits: no public source rebuilds the unique-user / round-trip split (the Intents explorer's stats live on Dune, which needs an API key), so "volume = adoption" remains unproven even though "volume" itself checks out. intents.near shows 156,790,097 lifetime transactions on NearBlocks — consistent with, but not a count of, the claimed 37M+ swaps.

claims.claim: NEAR has 46 million monthly active users
claims.test: Bound the true MAU from above in two windows: sum NearBlocks' daily active-account counts over the trailing 30 days, and over May 2025 — the month the claim's own source describes. A unique monthly count can never exceed either sum — if even the claim's own window falls below 46M, the claim is arithmetically impossible.

figures.label: Hard upper bound on MAU (Σ daily)
May 2025 ceiling, claim's own window (Σ daily)

claims.justification: Even the loosest possible bound kills this claim: summing every daily active-account count for the last 30 days (double-counting anyone active on two days) gives 1,746,682 — a true unique MAU is smaller still. The claim needs ~1,533,333 unique users per day; the chain shows ~58,223. Off by more than 26× against its own ceiling. And it fails in its own window too: the figure comes from May-2025 data, when the chain was ~7× busier — daily actives averaged 418,719 and peaked at 498,143 on 2025-05-20 — yet the same double-counting sum over all 31 days of May 2025 is 12,980,291, still 3.54× short of 46M. The claim was arithmetically impossible in the month it describes, not just today. (The 46M figure traces to May-2025 ecosystem marketing that counted cumulative/meta-transaction metrics as "users"; on-chain actives never came close.)

claims.claim: NEAR reached 1 million transactions per second
claims.claimant: Q4 2025 NEAR benchmark, validated in Nansen's quarterly report
claims.test: Compare the benchmark configuration (70 shards, pre-generated load) with production mainnet as it runs today: live TPS (NearBlocks), latest full-day average TPS (NearBlocks charts), and the shard count of a live block (RPC).
claims.justification: The 1M TPS figure is a documented benchmark on a 70-shard test configuration with pre-generated load — it survives as a lab result. As a network-capability headline it is inflated by ~96,504×: production mainnet runs 10 shards and sustains 6 TPS live (10.4 TPS averaged over the latest full day, 895,302 txns). Benchmark ≠ network.

claims.claimant: DataWallet, 'NEAR Protocol Statistics & Trends for 2026' (data as of 2026-09-22)
claims.test: Pull DefiLlama's own historical chain TVL for the claim's stated date and for today. A headline that overstates even its own cited source — and has since retraced — fails twice.
claims.justification: On the very date the article's data describes, its own cited source (DefiLlama) showed $197,227,814 — the headline overstates it by 19%. The level was genuinely reached later (peak $276,755,828 on 2026-10-12), so the claim is not fabricated — but it was published ahead of its evidence, and TVL has since retraced to $171,062,472. Quoted today without a date, it is false by $72.94M.

claims.claim: Confidential Intents holds $150M+ in confidential TVL with $3B+ in confidential volume
claims.claimant: NEAR Business product site / NEAR anniversary update, 2026-10-13
claims.test: Cross-check against the only independent aggregate that exists: DefiLlama's total Intents TVL (public + confidential, all chains). If no independent source can observe a confidential-only figure at all, the claim is structurally unverifiable.

figures.label: Share of total that must be confidential

claims.justification: Structurally unverifiable: the product's defining feature is that its flows are not publicly visible, and no independent aggregator separates confidential from public Intents TVL. The claim asks us to believe confidential TVL alone is ≥ $150M when ALL observable Intents TVL (public + confidential, every chain) totals $191,077,846 — i.e. 79% of everything would have to be confidential. Possible, but it rests entirely on the claimant's own say-so.
claims.missingData: A public/confidential split of NEAR Intents TVL and volume. DefiLlama reports only the combined total; the Intents explorer defers to Dune dashboards that require an API key; the confidential flows are not visible on-chain by design.

claims.claim: NEAR Intents has generated $52M+ in cumulative fees, with $8M+ directed to NEAR buybacks
claims.claimant: Nansen Q3 2026 report, relayed by CoinMarketCap, 2026-11-04
claims.test: Rebuild cumulative Intents fee revenue from DefiLlama's fees series and compare with $52M; assess whether the buyback leg has any independent public accounting (fees retained or reinvested are not buybacks).
claims.justification: The fees headline survives — and is even conservative: DefiLlama rebuilds cumulative NEAR Intents fees at $59,709,519, 15% ABOVE the claimed $52M. Reported separately because it does not follow from the fees number: the "$8M+ directed to NEAR buybacks" leg has no independent public accounting in any probed source (fees retained or reinvested are indistinguishable from buybacks without a disclosed buyback address), so that sub-claim stands unverified even though the headline figure holds.

claims.claim: NEAR mainnet runs 10 shards with 600ms blocks at 100% uptime
claims.claimant: NEAR Protocol six-year mainnet anniversary update, 2026-10-13
claims.test: Block time and shard count are directly observable (NearBlocks avg_block_time; chunk count of a live block via RPC). For '100% uptime', sample block production across ~1.6M consecutive blocks via archival RPC: any multi-minute stall would show up as a blown-out seconds-per-block segment.
claims.justification: This one survives the bear test. Block time: NearBlocks reports 0.594s average (claim: 0.600s). Shards: a live block carries exactly 10 chunks = 10 shards. Uptime: an absolute like "100%" can only be sampled, never proven — across 8 consecutive 200,000-block segments (~10.7 days, heights 222,256,364–223,856,364) the slowest segment averaged 0.59s/block, leaving no room for a multi-minute stall anywhere in the window.

claims.claim: Rhea Finance surpassed $16B in cumulative volume and generated over $1M in revenue in 12 months
claims.claimant: Paragraph ecosystem analysis (12 months leading to September 2025)
claims.test: Rebuild from DefiLlama: cumulative DEX volume of Rhea Dex (the Ref Finance lineage) up to 2025-09-30, plus BOTH candidate meanings of 'revenue' for Oct 2024 – Sep 2025 — protocol revenue (the protocol's own take) and gross fees paid by users. A claim that only holds under the looser definition is inflated by relabelling.
claims.justification: Split verdict inside one claim. The volume leg survives outright: DefiLlama rebuilds cumulative Rhea (Ref lineage) volume at $16,497,683,150 by Sep 2025, 103.1% of the $16B claim. The revenue leg survives only by relabelling: "$1M+ revenue" is true of gross fees users paid ($2,469,640), but under DefiLlama's actual revenue metric — the protocol's own take — Rhea earned $493,924, just 49.4% of the claim. Calling gross fees "revenue" is the inflation.
